title: The timeline of an hour-long edit scrolls, zooms and redraws at 120 Hz with hundreds of clips
goal: On a long edit the timeline is where a person spends their time, and it is the part most likely to slow down as clips pile up: every clip bar, thumbnail strip and waveform drawn again when anything moves. Make the timeline of the 60 minute reference edit, several hundred clips, scroll, zoom and follow a playing playhead at the display's 120 Hz, and keep an edit on it inside one frame.
notes: Fourth success item of video-perf ('the timeline scrolls and zooms at 120 Hz with hundreds of clips'). Depends on the speed walk task a-speed-walk-measures-the-long-reference-edit-th; if that walk's ranking says the timeline is not where the time goes, say so in the log and narrow this to what it measured. Precedents for building only what is on screen: the-layers-list-only-builds-the-rows-you-can-see, the-layers-panel-only-draws-thumbnails-for-the-r, keying-a-value-redraws-only-what-the-key-changes (all done). Timeline code: TimelineTrackRows.swift, ClipPiecesBar.swift (104 KB), TimelineDock.swift, SoundLane.swift; 23 app files read editorState.documentTimeMS. The playhead belongs on its own layer, not in the clip rows' bodies.
acceptance: Measured first with the speed walk on the 60 minute reference edit at Next defaults: frame times scrolling and zooming the timeline end to end, view bodies rebuilt per playback frame, and the longest main thread pass for trim, move, blade and undo. Numbers in the audit before any change.
Scrolling and zooming the 60 minute timeline: no frame over 8.3 ms on the main thread (120 Hz) in 95 percent of frames and none over 16 ms, measured by the speed walk.

While it plays with nothing being edited, only the playhead and what the playhead changes are rebuilt each frame: clip bars, thumbnails and waveforms off screen or unchanged are not built again (counted with ViewBuildMeter, the count in the audit before and after).
Trim, move, blade and undo on the 60 minute edit each finish within 16 ms on the main thread, as on the 6 minute one.
No change in what the timeline shows: the timeline walks that photograph it (cut, trim, transitions, key lanes) stay green. Perf numbers before and after in the audit; Scripts/test.sh passes.
Audit written under queue/audits/. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Speed walk baseline (2026-11-12) on the 6 minute edit, before any change: zooming the timeline in and out ran at a median 477 ms a frame (42 frames in 20 s, every one late against 8.3 ms), scrolling end to end 392 ms a frame (p95 490 ms); playing untouched, the dock's body (inspectorPanel) built once per new picture and the Time section every other one. The 60 minute numbers are in this task's audit (queue/audits/2026-11-13-speed-walk.json). The cost under them is the same trackLayout() rebuilt per query (isCutLocked -> isClipOnLockedTrack in the timeline). Measure with Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --long 60 (timeline step).

From a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed (2026-11-13): the document now keeps its track layout and edit points (DocumentDerived.swift), and timeline right-click menus no longer rebuild every tick (EditorState.timelineMenuRows). 20 min edit after: zoom 489 ms a frame (was 2515), scroll 207 ms (was 2003), edits 212-428 ms (were 2.8-29.8 s). Time Profiler playing the 6 min edit: ~86% of the main thread is SwiftUI graph work after each playhead move (ObservationGraphMutation ~15%, AccessibilityViewGraph 8-12%), few bodies rebuilt (ViewBodyAccessor ~4%): something high in the window is dirtied each tick and SwiftUI re-checks everything under it.

triage 2026-11-13, seen in queue/audits/2026-11-13-long-edit-plays-after-the-edits-sc.png: on the 6 minute reference edit the timeline stacks a separate 'Zoom' lane under V1 for each zoomed clip (three show, more below the fold), each nearly empty, with bars around 5:30 while the picked clip is at 0:24. The reference edit zooms every third clip, so the 60 minute one carries well over a hundred such lanes: count them, measure what they cost the timeline's redraw, and say in the audit whether a long edit's zooms should share fewer lanes (the zoom mock, video-zoom-wt.html, draws a picked clip's Scale and Centre lanes, not one per clip for the whole edit). Not filed on its own: unconfirmed whether every zoomed clip always gets its lane.
